tokenEvents.label: User access token
tokenEvents.explanation:
Issued by PingOne after Authorization Code + PKCE login. Stored in the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) session (server-side httpOnly cookie — never sent to the browser). Token carries 5 scope(s): ai:agent:read read openid admin:read write
✓ Agent scopes: ai:agent:read

tokenEvents.label: ID token (OpenID Connect)
tokenEvents.explanation: Issued by PingOne at login when the openid scope is granted. Proves the user's identity to the BFF (the relying party): aud is the BFF client_id, and claims like auth_time and acr describe how and when the user authenticated. Held in the BFF session and used for OIDC sign-off — it is NOT a bearer for API calls (that is the access token above) and never reaches the browser.

tokenEvents.label: Refresh token (RFC 6749 §1.5)
tokenEvents.explanation: Issued by PingOne at login when the offline_access scope is granted. An OPAQUE credential (not a JWT — no claims to decode) used to silently mint new access tokens when the current one expires (RFC 6749 §6). Held server-side in the BFF session and never sent to the browser; the token value is intentionally not shown here.

tokenEvents.label: User Token — PingOne Active-Token Introspection at Login (RFC 7662)
tokenEvents.explanation: PingOne confirmed the user token is active at login. sub=85abea5b-70a9-4d50-9250-1d5366bfa5d2 scope="ai:agent:read,read,openid,admin:read,write". Introspection is called once per login and cached in the session.

tokenEvents.label: Token exchange (RFC 8693): user access token → MCP access token
tokenEvents.explanation: Your session has a user access token (above). The exchange runs when the AI Agent invokes a banking tool. For high-value and transfer transactions, the exchange is paired with human-in-the-loop consent (HITL).

tokenEvents.label: MCP access token (delegated) → MCP server
tokenEvents.explanation: After a successful exchange on an MCP tool call, decoded MCP access token claims (including act, audience, and scope) appear here.
